eMOLT Update 2026-08-14

At the end of last week, Erin, Huanxin, and cooperative research legend JiM Manning joined the Northeast Fisheries Science Center team for the Woods Hole Science Stroll. Over 1,300 people visited the NEFSC’s Woods Hole Lab to check out some of the research we have going on. In addition to the eMOLT/drifter crew, the Cooperative Research Branch team was represented by Ben Church, Giovanni Gianesin, Dave McElroy, Julie Nieland, and Heather Soulen who showcased the new mackerel research initiative and the Gulf of Maine Bottom Longline Survey.

A) Huanxin Xu from the Gulf of Maine Lobster Foundation explains how an eMOLT system works. B) George Maynard from the Northeast Fisheries Science Center describes a monkfish. C) Dave McElroy from the NEFSC demonstrates otolith extraction from a haddock.

This week, the eMOLT fleet recorded 152 tows of sensorized fishing gear totaling 7224 sensor hours underwater. Bottom temps remain close to last year’s values in the Gulf of Maine and Southern New England and are slightly cooler than last year in the Mid-Atlantic and on Georges Bank.

FISHBOT bottom temperature records from the past week. The data are available on the Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation ERDDAP and an interactive visualization is available at the Cape Cod Ocean Watch dashboard hosted by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. FISHBOT aggregates data provided by participants in eMOLT, the CFRF Lobster and Jonah Crab Research Fleet, the CFRF Shelf Research Fleet, the Cape Cod Commercial Fishermen’s Alliance Cape Cod Oceanographic Research Fleet, the Maine Coast Fishermen’s Association Fisheries Ocean Data Program, MassDMF Cape Cod Bay Study Fleet, the Northeast Fisheries Science Center Study Fleet, and the Northeast Fisheries Science Center Ecosystem Monitoring Surveys

Dissolved Oxygen

Dissolved oxygen levels remain high around Isle Au Haut, in Casco Bay, and in Cape Cod Bay (screenshot from Massachusetts DMF’s Cape Cod Bay dashboard below). One low reading (4.6 mg/L) occurred off Scusset Beach earlier in the week, but nearby sensors are still reading normal values. At the mouth of Narragansett Bay, readings collected by CFRF partner vessels remain in the “Very Low” category, around 2.9 mg/L, a decline from last week.

Bottom Temperature Forecast Performance

Bottom temperature observations were generally warmer than forecast by either model Downeast, cooler than forecast by either model in Massachusetts Bay and Cape Cod Bay, and warmer than forecast by either model along the shelf break.

> Comparisons between bottom temperatures predicted by two ocean forecasting models and observations from the eMOLT fleet. Blue dots show where the observations were cooler than the forecast and red dots show where the observations were warmer than the forecast. White dots show areas where the observations and forecasts agreed. On the left is the comparison with the Doppio model and on the right is the comparison with the NECOFS model (GOM7).

National Ocean Service to Deploy NECOFS as an Operational Forecast Model

In an effort to improve efficiency and provide seamless geographic coverage for forecasting water levels, currents, temperature, and salinity throughout the region, the National Ocean Service will deploy the Northeast Coast Operational Forecast System (NECOFS) to their production servers in the near future. This deployment will coincide with the decommissioning of four operational forecast systems (Gulf of Maine Operational Forecast System, Port of New York and New Jersey Operational Forecast System, Delaware Bay Operational Forecast System, and Chesapeake Bay Operational Forecast System).

The map above shows the NECOFS grid (black) and bounding boxes (orange and red) representing the spatial coverage of the systems it is replacing. The NOS version of NECOFS will be slightly different from the version currently presented in this newsletter (which is a development version from the University of Massachusetts). As the new forecast system comes online, we will work to develop scripts to compare it with the eMOLT data, the same way we do for the development version of NECOFS and Doppio now. Some example experimental forecast products from the development version are shown below. You can explore more here. We’ll keep you up to date when the production version goes live.
